conventions.$comment: frameworkPaths belong to NO flag: they are shared infrastructure serving every flag, so they never count as owned code nor as touch points. Matched as path fragments, which is why the backend entry has no src/ prefix — it also covers src-test/.

features.$knownGapComment: USER-ACCEPTED VISIBLE DEBT (scorecard demo). src/com/etendoerp/go/payment/TenantPlanService.java. markProductive: zero coverage — the paid-plan marker is entirely unexercised. resolvePlan: only the exception-swallow path executes (returns 'free' on failure); every distinguishing path (preference found productive/other, null query, blank-clientId guard) is untested. The only covered branch is the one that hides failures — exactly how a paying tenant would silently appear free. Coverage arrives transitively, not deliberately: EtendoGoJwtDalHelper holds a static TenantPlanService (line 72), so EtendoGoJwtDalHelperTest.BuildEnvironmentJson calls resolvePlan, its unstubbed Preference query NPEs into the catch, and reportsFreePlanWithoutMarker asserts the resulting 'free'. The unit spec below is declared acceptedDebt and is intentionally not being written, so this flag carries a per-item tests penalty on purpose rather than reading as a clean sheet. Asserting the AD_Preference persistence itself stays integration scope and is NOT what the deferred unit spec would cover.

deferredItems.note: The two ends bucket users on different identities: the frontend sends localStorage.sf_auth_user (the ERP admin username) as OpenFeature's targetingKey, while the backend targets the account email. Harmless today because the local InMemoryProvider ignores the targeting key entirely, and a CORRECTNESS BLOCKER the moment a targeting-aware control plane lands — wiring Mixpanel first would bake per-user bucketing divergence into live rollouts, where it is invisible in aggregate. Must be closed BEFORE the swap, not after.

deferredItems.note: The paid flow is a mock: MockPaymentService checks the token's SHAPE, nothing is charged, and no gateway exists. The components split by TRIGGER. Gateway-triggered — gap-replay, gap-check-then-act, gap-payment-provisioning-atomicity, and qa-in-flight-submit-guard — are latent until money is real (the last one can already duplicate a tenant, but only by script; a human double-click cannot reach it). Flag-on — qa-navigation-guard, qa-clientname-unbounded and qa-session-expiry-reported-late — bite as soon as the flag is enabled for anyone, gateway or not: they are UX and validation defects in a flow users can complete today. Bundled because they share one owner decision and one review moment, not because they share a trigger. PROMOTION CONDITION (Alex, review of a7cb81333): if the flag ever pilots before a gateway exists, the three flag-on components must be promoted to their own deferredItem — at that point they are scheduled work, not part of the real-payments decision, and the bundle-a-theme-split-a-schedule rule applies.

components.note: QA #2 — no in-flight guard on submit: 8 scripted same-tick clicks produce 8 POSTs with 8 tokens. handleSubmit (UpgradePage.jsx:273) sets no submitting state and the button is never disabled. A human double-click cannot reproduce it; a real charge per POST would make it expensive.
QA #3 — nothing guards navigation mid-provisioning: back or refresh is silent, with copy as the only mitigation. No beforeunload handler and no router blocker anywhere in the page.

QA #4 — clientName is unbounded on BOTH ends: no maxLength on the input, and parseOnboardingRequest rejects only the empty string. An oversized name passes the paywall and fails deep inside provisioning, i.e. after the point where a real charge would have been taken.

QA #5 — session expiry is known at mount but reported only after the form is filled: the mount effect reads the platform token, yet on 'unavailable' the checkout is still rendered, so the user completes card details before being told the session is gone.
Module doc — the token is never consumed, so one approved payment can create N tenants. Needs the token marked spent or bound to a single tenant creation.

Module doc — the paywall reads ownership and provisioning creates the client afterwards with no lock between: two concurrent POST /sws/go/onboarding calls both pass the gate. Needs an atomic check-and-create or a uniqueness constraint that catches the loser.

Module doc — no atomicity between payment and provisioning: the paywall passes, provisioning then fails, its catch rolls back the DAL changes, and with a real gateway that is a captured charge with no tenant and no refund, retry-with-credit or idempotency path. Distinct from qa-clientname-unbounded, which is merely its easiest trigger: bounding the input closes the trigger, not the gap. Needs authorize-before-provision with capture on success, or a compensating refund.

features.$deferredItemsComment: Open items this flag carries that are NOT test gaps. Scored per item by kind (a deferred decision is a standing decision, same reasoning as an accepted-debt spec) and rendered on the flag's card, so the TTL surfaces them before the work they block starts rather than during it. A bundled item costs its kind plus one per component beyond the first; promote a component to its own item once it gets scheduled separately.

features.description: Per-flag technical debt scorer: the flags-registry contract, the sf-flag-debt CLI and the feature-debt workflow that make debt visible per feature.
features.$pathsComment: Deliberately empty: the scorer's owned code (cli/src/flag-debt.js and cli/test/flag-debt.test.js) lives in schema_forge_core, which no registry root can reach — evidence #1 for the multi-repo-registry-split item below. ETP-4697 is also what lets this entry declare its real paths and specs.

deferredItems.note: The registry model is single-repo plus vendored backend: schema_forge_core code cannot register flags at all, the score is checkout-dependent (resolveRoots silently counts backend specs as pending when the module checkout is absent — same commit, different score), and SONAR_PROJECT_BY_ROOT hardcodes two Sonar projects. Therefore any core feature ships with unmeasured debt and worktree scores cannot be trusted until the split lands. Fix: three per-repo registries (header/contribution) + sf-flag-debt --rollup with merge-then-score semantics. User-accepted 2026-07-28 (kickoff proceeds on the v2 format; migration is mechanical). PROMOTION CONDITION: the moment any component is scheduled as its own task, it becomes its own deferredItem.
